newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN PUBLIC SECTOR CHANGE IN 'CHAOS' - COSATU.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN PUBLIC SECTOR CHANGE IN 'CHAOS' - COSATU.

text.p: The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) said on Tuesday the transformation of the country's public sector was disorderly and failing to meet expectations.
"My impression, and it is shared by the public sector unions, is that it is in chaos," Zwelinzima Vavi, the federation's assistant secretary general, told a news briefing.
"I don't believe it is going according to any expectations that I can have in terms of what we should have already achieved in the whole process of public sector transformation," he said.
Vavi said too little emphasis had been placed on delivering services in the rush to slim down the public sector to meet a target reduction of 7,000 jobs by 1999.

Cosatu general secretary Sam Shilowa told the briefing that while the unions did not want to recklessly boot out whites from the public sector, an official skills audit should be carried out to assess how blacks could be promoted into senior posts.
"We don't want to have a reckless situation where we want to retrench whites just because they are white males -- but at the same time we don't have to be coy," he said.
President Nelson Mandela's government wants to change the face of the old white-dominated public sector to reflect its three-year-old multiracial democracy.

However, it is hampered by a "sunset clause" agreement which secures the jobs of white bureaucrats for at least five years. The deal, struck before the historic 1994 elections, helped ensure a peaceful handover of power to Mandela's African National Congress.
